Overview

In AION 2 dungeons the Cleric is a healer that has to deal damage: rewards depend on your contribution, and a Cleric who only heals can walk out with nothing. Your party has plenty of dodges and invulnerabilities of its own — top people up after hits, and put everything else into damage.

  • You are paid for damage. Dungeon rewards depend on your contribution, so a Cleric who only heals can leave with nothing — this whole build is about dealing damage while healing on the side.

The build in one sentence

Earth Punishment makes Condemnation always crit, and a crit resets Condemnation — so it fires with no cooldown, while Divine Aura, Bolt and Noble Aura add damage on top.

This mode follows Kaeria's Cleric PvE video guide (Russian, recorded on the Taiwan client on September 28; she says it applies to global too), checked against the video frames on September 30, and against Lucia's guide (English, global, October 5 — a World's First Rank 1 Cleric at 2,160 item level). Skill picks are reversible for free — only arcana cost resources.

Patch Season 1. The build is checked against guides from the global servers: 4 stigmas, cap 20.

Overview

In PvP the Cleric keeps the PvE core — Condemnation reset by crits, Judgment Thunder, the heals — and changes what the stigmas and a few picks are for: crowd control, cutting the enemy's healing, and keeping the party alive through a burst.

The build in one sentence

Buff with Prayer of Amplification and Light of Protection, put Voice of Doom on the healer or the tank you are killing, and save Yustiel's Power for the moment the enemy bursts.

This mode follows the PvP part of Lucia's Cleric guide (English, global, October 5 — a World's First Rank 1 Cleric): stigmas for duels and group fights and the picks she changes for PvP. She promised a separate video on PvP combos; until then the rotation is the PvE one.

Passives

  • Empyrean Lord's Grace — the most important one: Critical Damage, Double Chance and extra damage on every hit. As high as you can.
  • Earth's Grace — used to buff the party, now only you; still worth leveling.
  • Healing Enhancement — heal boost as a share of your Attack, so a Cleric builds Attack rather than Defense.
  • Radiant Benediction — heals nearby allies on attacks; take it if you go all-in on damage.
  • Warm Benediction and Immortal Veil are fine to have; Empyrean Lords' Benediction is for PvP.

Lucia levels these three first, before any other passive: Empyrean Lord's Grace, Healing Enhancement and Earth's Grace. Immortal Veil helps early and falls off once your armor scales.

First days (aLuckyRO): level Radiant Benediction — it heals the whole party every few seconds while they hit — and Healing Enhancement first. The crit passives pay off only once your gear gives Critical Hit; until then you barely crit.

Gear & stats

  • Gear lines: Might (attack and heal), Combat Speed, Damage Boost; Weapon Damage Boost and Precision are strong too. Skip status resists, evasion and defensive lines in PvE.
  • Weapon and guard (Lucia): Weapon Damage Boost, Might, Combat Speed, Precision. Gloves: Combat Speed; boots: Movement Speed. Accessories: Combat Speed, Might and Precision, plus one line for Earth's Grace or Empyrean Lord's Grace.
  • Rings: craft them as soon as you can — crafted rings have one more line for active skills. Fill every line with active skills: Condemnation, Radiant Recovery, Judgment Thunder, and Healing Light or Divine Aura.
  • Stats: Destruction, Wisdom (Double Chance), Illusion (cooldowns), Time (Combat Speed), Freedom (accuracy), plus Death (Critical Hit) — Kaeria's own pick, a Cleric is always short on crit; Might, Precision, Constitution. Lucia's four: Time, Illusion, Space, Destruction.
  • For the Ludra raid: at least 1,000 Accuracy and 1,000 Critical Hit.
  • Wings: Talisra Wings (Attack 60, Defense 400, Accuracy 35, −4% cooldowns) from the season shop for about 250,000 season points — save the points for them.

Genus Insight

Get every pet to level 3 early: killing pets you have leveled gives the crystals for these lines. Lucia's picks for each wheel:

SlotTake
1, 5Attack Bonus (5: or Max Attack)
2, 8HP
3, 6, 9Accuracy, or Block if your accuracy is already high
4The damage line of that wheel: Damage Boost, Perfect Chance, Back Attack Damage
7Regeneration or Endurance
SpecialDouble Chance

Roll for the highest value and lock a line only when it is close to the maximum — and never before the wheel is level 9–10.

Titles — which one to equip in each slot: After level 45 → Titles. Pets and Genus Insight — what to level and what to roll at 10: Pets → Genus Insight.

Gear & stats

  • Gear lines as in PvE — Weapon Damage Boost, Might, Combat Speed, Precision on the weapon and guard; accessories Combat Speed, Might, Precision.
  • Genus Insight: Critical Hit Resist instead of HP on slot 2, and Front Attack Damage Boost on the damage slot of that wheel — in PvP you face the target.
  • Azphel, the level-45 Daevanion board, is all PvP Damage Boost and Tolerance — fill it for PvP.

Set bonuses: collect 2 + 2, or four cards of Primal Vigor (+60 PvE Attack with two, +150 with four, while your HP is 70% or more). Early on a card with the right skills beats a card from the right set — fix the sets later.

Daevanion boards

Daevanion takes your skills from 10 to 14 and adds stats. Each blue node gives +1 level to its skill.

  • Priority: orange Cooldown and Combat Speed nodes first, then Attack and Critical, then the blue skill nodes, then the defensive orange nodes, passives last.
  • Critical Damage Tolerance and Multi-Hit Resist do nothing in PvE — bosses don't crit or multi-hit.
  • Resetting a board is cheap, and you will rebuild it many times.
  • Lucia's order: on Nezekan and Zikel take all four corners and your skills; on Vaizel and Triniel skip the corners and go straight for the active skills you use.
  • Whelps' order: first the blue nodes that take your active skills to 12 — the second specialization slot is a big power spike; then the orange attack nodes (Combat Speed, Cooldown Reduction, Damage Boost, Critical Damage Boost, Multi-Hit Chance), the Empyrean Lord's Grace and Earth's Grace nodes, Attack and Critical, and only then the defensive ones (Damage Tolerance, Critical Damage Tolerance, HP, Defense). Avoid the MP +50 nodes where you can.
  • Azphel (level 45) is all PvP Damage Boost and Tolerance — take it for PvP.
  • No Ariel on global: there are five boards, and the level-45 one, Azphel, gives only PvP Damage Boost and Tolerance — in PvE finish the first four.

  • Levels 12–45: Daevanion Crystal ×136.

With a Chanter in the party: replace Light of Protection with Absolution, another heal or Summon Resurrection. Voice of Doom (−200 Critical Hit Resist on the boss at 15) is an option in sanctuaries with a second healer, mostly early while everyone is short on crit; Power Burst only where the stagger bar has to be broken and nobody else can do it (Nightmare). Root and Assault Mark have no use in PvE.

Whelps: level Earth Punishment to 20 first, then the others evenly, Light of Protection last. For a support role swap Noble Aura for Summon Resurrection or Yustiel's Power; with a Chanter swap Light of Protection for one of them. He keeps two skill presets, with and without a Chanter — each preset holds its own skill levels.

270 × Stigma Shard — from the shops, plus a few for levels and the story where they come from
  • Abyss shop: Stigma Shard ×50 per step, four steps per character (200 in all) — Abyss Points ×10,000, 15,000, 20,000 and 25,000 each.
  • Nightmare Shop (Growth tab): Stigma Shard ×35 per character for Phantasmal Fragment ×1,500 each — 52,500 in total.
  • Shugo Festival Shop: Stigma Shard ×35 per character for Centuryroot Token ×300 each — 10,500 in total.
  • Levels and the main story give a few more.

Macro

?The macro key is not bound by default: bind it in Settings → Key Settings → General → Macro. Bind it to RMB — then you hold it together with the basic attack on LMB.

Lucia's global setup: only the in-game macro, two steps, and two hotbar lines read from her hotbar (frame 13:10). In AION 2 the bottom slot of a line has the highest priority; the cards show each line top to bottom as in the game.

  • Lower ping than on Taiwan: animations cancel better, so the macro can weave more basic attacks.

1. Hotbar lines

  2. 3 Chain of Torment
  3. 2 Earth Punishment
  4. 1 Prayer of Amplification

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

Prayer whenever it is ready, then Earth Punishment and Chain of Torment, so every Condemnation crits and resets. Keep Light of Protection out of the line: it is a toggle, and every second press would switch it off.

TDivine Aura line
  1. 2 Judgment Thunder
  2. 1 Divine Aura

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

The aura when it is ready, Judgment Thunder in between — after each Judgment Thunder Condemnation can crit and reset again.

Outside the macro — the rest of her bar:

Lightning Strike Scattershot on a staggered boss, otherwise Debilitating Mark — press it on cooldown.

  2. 1 Light of Regeneration

In-game order, top to bottom. 1 = highest priority — the bottom slot.

Light of Regeneration whenever it is ready, Healing Light (three charges) for the rest.

On RMB, every step with a 10 ms delay:

  1. 1Prayer linePrayer of Amplification

  • By handThe Debuff line on cooldown; the Heal line and Radiant Recovery when someone just took a hit; fully charged Bolt; Noble Aura on cooldown.

Lucia notes that a third-party macro does more, but she sticks to the in-game one.

Recap

  • Skills: Condemnation, Radiant Recovery, Divine Aura, Bolt 16 → 20; Judgment Thunder, Lightning Strike Scattershot, Healing Light 16; the rest 12–14.
  • Stigmas: Earth Punishment, Light of Protection, Prayer of Amplification (all three to 20), Noble Aura; with a Chanter swap Light of Protection for Absolution.
  • Play: deal damage for contribution; heal only the people who just got hit.

Recap

  • Skills: as in PvE; Chain of Torment and Debilitating Mark take their crowd-control picks, Earth's Retribution ignores Block and Evasion at 20.
  • Stigmas: Prayer of Amplification, Light of Protection, Yustiel's Power, Voice of Doom; in group PvP Absolution instead of Voice of Doom.
  • Gear: PvE lines; Critical Hit Resist and Front Attack Damage on Genus Insight, the Azphel board.

Overview

The Cleric is the healer, but while leveling it plays as a ranged damage dealer: Chain of Torment marks the target, Condemnation punishes it, and the passive Radiant Benediction heals you and the party on every hit. Heal only when you need to.

Leveling in one sentence

Hold Earth's Retribution for mana, spam the Chain line with the in-game macro, and put your skill points into attacks rather than heals.

Patch Season 1. The build is checked against guides from the global servers: 4 stigmas, cap 20.

How to fight while leveling

  • Packs: Chain of Torment (hits up to 4) → Condemnation → Divine Aura with the AoE pick → Judgment Thunder.
  • Elites: Debilitating Mark (lower Defense) → Chain of Torment → Bolt charged → Condemnation.
  • Mana: target mode, and weave Earth's Retribution — it restores MP on every cast.
  • Low HP: Healing Light, and Radiant Benediction keeps ticking as long as you hit.
  • Staggered bosses: Lightning Strike Scattershot only works while the target is staggered.
  • Skill points: the attack skills first, heals later; spare points go into Empyrean Lord's Grace and Earth's Grace (Whelps).
